member: Tomas - Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Analyst
message:
Elena, Marcus, Priya, comfort for this bridge must be judged against French footbridge guide (Setra) and Human-induced Vibration of Steel Structures (HiVoSS) classes in the Experimental and Numerical Study on Dynamics of Two Footbridges with Different Shapes of Girders (E38) and the COMPDYN 2015 (E39). Maximum comfort needs below 0.500 m/s2 and minimum comfort needs below 1.00 m/s2, with above 2.50 m/s2 unacceptable, and the 1.90 Hz mode sits inside the 1.25 Hz to 2.30 Hz critical range in the Microsoft Word - Geradin_JRC_Design of Footbridges_150909.doc (E44) so resonant walking governs.

Elena, Marcus, Priya, the deciding crowd is a dense crowd at 0.500 pedestrians per square metre in the Vibration Serviceability Assessment of a Historic Suspension Footbridge (E41) reduced by the equivalent-synchronized rule in the 4.4.1 Dynamic load cases - Footbridge guide setra (E42). Tuned Mass Damper (TMD, a secondary mass tuned to the bridge mode) scale comes from the modal stiffness from 20 tonne modal mass at 1.9 Hz (E11), where one 280 N resonant walker already gives 1.75 m/s2, equal to 0.178 times gravity (g, acceleration of free fall), clearly bouncy.

Elena, Marcus, Priya, with the 500 kg mass in the TMD mass from 2.5 percent ratio (E22), the Resonant response with and without TMD to estimate comfort reduction (E47) drops that walker to 0.103 m/s2, equal to 0.0105 g and barely felt, with 3.80 mm relative motion, about a fingernail width. I am ready, because the hidden damper restores maximum comfort without changing the deck look.
